newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northeast spot power mixed after recent gains.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northeast spot power mixed after recent gains.

text.p: Spot electricity prices in the northeastern U.S. finished mixed Thursday after recent gains tied to a high-voltage line outage and talks of reduced operation at a New York nuclear power plant.
The outage of the 345 kilovolt (KV) line in central New York cut capacity of the Central-East Interface by 1,000 megawatt (MW). That transmission junction usually has a capacity of 2,600-2,700 MW.
The maintenance shutdown of the 345 kilovolt (KV) line, operated by Niagara Mohawk Power Corp, began Monday and was planned to restart late Friday.
Eastern and southern New York utilities switched on expensive fossil-fired generation to compensated for reduced supply from western New York.
There were lingering talks of reduced operation at the 1,137 megawatt (MW) Nine Mile Point nuclear power unit 2 in Scriba, N.Y., to repair of a circulation pump.

NIMO, the operator of Nine Mile Point 2, was still trying to determine whether to merely reduce output from the Scriba, N.Y., unit, or to shut it outright to perform other repairs as well, market sources said.
"It's unclear right now whether it'd be reduced tomorrow, or be shut all the way through next week," one trade source said.

In the eastern portion of the New York Power Pool (NYPP), trading of peak, non-firm electricity for Friday was pegged at $31.00-$34.00 a megawatt hour (MWh), off from Wednesday's notational mid-$30.00 range.
Off-peak, non-firm power for Friday in eastern NYPP was again steady at $19.00-$20.00.
The lack of buying interest today pressured prices lower, market sources said.
In the western NYPP, peak, non-firm electricity prices for Thursday rose again in tandem with stronger next-day prices at the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) Interconnect pool.
Western NYPP power for peak, non-firm delivery on Friday was quoted at $23.00-$25.00, firmer than Wednesday's $22.75-$23.25 for Thursday.
Western NYPP power for non-firm delivery during light load hours on Friday edged up to $14.50-$15.00 versus Wednesday's $14.25-$14.75.
Spot power prices in the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), peak, non-firm electricity for Friday at the Northeast Utilities border was quoted in the $31.00-$33.00, off from $35.50-$36.50 Wednesday.
Non-firm, off-peak NEPOOL power for Friday delivery to the NU border remained in the $19.50-$20.50 range.

Friday's temperatures in most of the Northeast were predicted to peak in 20-40s Fahrenheit and bottom in the teens to 20s. A cooling trend was forecast later this week with temperatures falling two to six degrees below normal Monday.
